title: Canva guide for small business owners
description: A step-by-step guide to free Canva: a promotional image in 10 minutes, posters, menus, marketplace product photos, AI tools and when Canva Pro is worth it.
author: Cross Tech Edu
cover_alt: A bakery owner using Canva on a laptop to design a 20% off weekend promotion
body:
**Canva** is an online design tool that lets you make promotional images, posters, menus and product photos by **picking a ready-made template and dragging things around**. No Photoshop, no designer needed for everyday graphics, and the free plan covers most of what a small shop needs.

This Canva guide is written for people who have never designed anything: the layout of the editor, a promotional image in 10 minutes, posters and product photos, Canva's AI tools, common mistakes, and when the paid plan is worth it.

## 1. What can free Canva do?

A free account gives you:

- **Millions of templates** for Facebook, Instagram and TikTok posts, posters, menus, business cards and online-shop banners.
- **Free photos, icons and fonts**, including many fonts that handle Vietnamese accents.
- **Downloads** as PNG, JPG or print-ready PDF.
- **AI tools** for writing copy and generating images, with a monthly usage allowance.
- **Computer and phone apps** that sync your designs automatically.

Templates and images marked with a **crown icon** belong to Canva Pro (paid). Some handy features, such as **one-click background removal** and **automatic resizing**, are Pro-only too.

Canva is one of the [6 free AI tools for small businesses](/en/blog/free-ai-tools-for-small-business/) we have covered, and the only one focused on images and print.

## 2. Signing up and finding your way around

1. Go to **canva.com** on a computer or install the **Canva** app (developer: Canva) on your phone.
2. Sign up with **Continue with Google** to use your Gmail account; no new password needed.
3. When asked what you'll use Canva for, choose **small business** or **personal**. It only affects which templates Canva suggests.

The editor has three main areas:

| Area | What it's for |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Left panel** | Templates, text, photos, icons, and uploading your own pictures |
| **Centre** | The design itself; click any text or image to edit it |
| **Top bar** | Font, size and colour; the **Share** button to download |

## 3. A promotional image in 10 minutes

Example: a *"20% off this weekend"* image for a bakery's Facebook page.

### Step 1: Pick the right size

On the home page, search for **"Facebook post"** (or "Instagram post", "TikTok"). Canva opens a canvas at the right size, so nothing gets cropped when you post.

### Step 2: Choose a template

Search the left panel for **"sale"** or **"promotion"**. Choose a layout you like; colours can be changed later.

### Step 3: Replace text, photos and colours

- **Double-click the text** and type your own: offer, dates, address or phone number.
- **Drag your product photo** from your uploads onto the template photo to replace it.
- Click a coloured block and pick your **brand colour**.

### Step 4: Check and download

Re-read the price, dates and phone number. Click **Share** → **Download** and choose **PNG** for the sharpest result on social media.

> **Tip:** once you have an image you like, **duplicate the design** for your next offer and just change the words. Your posts will look consistent and more professional.

## 4. Posters, menus and product photos

### Posters and menus for printing

Search for **"menu"** or **"poster"**. When downloading for print, choose **PDF Print**. Ask your print shop for the paper size (A4, A3) first and pick it from the start.

### Product photos for online marketplaces

Marketplaces such as Shopee and TikTok Shop favour **square photos with a clean background and the product in the centre**. With the free plan:

1. Photograph the product against a **plain background** (a sheet of white A3 paper, a light wall) in good daylight.
2. In Canva, create a square design (for example 1080 × 1080).
3. Place the photo and add a frame, a price tag or a small *"Free shipping"* label in a corner.

If you need to remove backgrounds for dozens of products every week, that's when Pro's background remover pays for itself.

### Business cards, vouchers and small signs

Search by name (**"business card"**, **"voucher"**) and edit them exactly like the promotional image above.

## 5. Using AI in Canva

Canva has a set of AI tools inside the editor:

- **Writing help:** headlines, taglines and short product descriptions.
- **Text to image:** type *"strawberry cake on a wooden table, warm light"* to get an illustration.
- **Design suggestions:** describe what you need and Canva proposes a few layouts.

The free plan includes **a limited number of AI uses per month**; when they run out, wait for next month or upgrade.

> **Note:** AI images are fine for decoration and backgrounds. **Don't use them in place of real product photos**: customers who receive something different lose trust, and marketplaces may penalise the listing.

## 6. Common mistakes and how to avoid them

- **Broken Vietnamese accents:** switch fonts. Type a test phrase with accents before you commit to a font.
- **Text too small on phones:** most customers scroll on a phone. Use a big headline and one main message per image.
- **Accidentally using Pro elements:** items with a crown can't be downloaded on the free plan without paying. Canva usually tells you which item is Pro when you download, so you can swap it out.
- **Using other brands' assets:** don't put other companies' logos or famous cartoon characters in your sales images without permission.
- **Wrong details:** check prices, dates and phone numbers. One wrong number on 500 printed flyers costs real money.

## 7. When to upgrade to Canva Pro

The free plan is enough if you make a few social posts a week. Consider **Canva Pro** when:

- You need to **remove backgrounds** from many product photos.
- You want **one design resized automatically** for Facebook, Instagram and TikTok.
- You want a **brand kit** (logo, colours, fonts) saved so staff use them correctly.
- You regularly run out of AI uses.

In Vietnam, Canva Pro for one person costs around **150,000 VND a month** at the time of writing, less if you pay yearly. Check the current price on Canva's site before buying. Only pay Canva directly, and **never buy a cheap "Canva Pro account"** from a stranger: you can be removed from the shared team at any time and lose your designs.

## 8. Where to start

1. **Today:** sign up and make one promotional image following the 4 steps in section 3.
2. **This week:** photograph your 3 best-selling products on a plain background and make square marketplace images.
3. **At the weekend:** save a "standard" design for your shop (colours, fonts, logo position) so next time you only change the text.

Canva handles the visuals; for the words, an AI assistant helps, see our [ChatGPT guide for business owners](/en/blog/chatgpt-guide-for-small-business-owners/). To turn product photos into short videos, read the [CapCut guide for sales videos](/en/blog/capcut-guide-for-small-business-videos/).

*Checked in October 2026. Canva updates its layout and plans fairly often, so button names may differ slightly from this guide.*
